outcome_detail: $7.5 million settlement approved by the Chisago County Board of Commissioners on February 18, 2026, paid through the Minnesota Counties Intergovernmental Trust in exchange for dismissal of the lawsuit and release of claims. The settlement followed a ruling by U.S. District Judge Katherine Menendez that the county could face Monell liability for Duncan's conduct and the court's December 2025 denial of the county's motion to certify an interlocutory appeal.
criminal_detail: Duncan was charged in 2022 with two counts of third-degree and three counts of fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct over the 2017 scheme. In November 2023 he pleaded guilty to one count of third-degree criminal sexual conduct; in February 2024 he was sentenced to 178 days in the Washington County jail, 15 years of probation with a stayed 57-month prison term, $700 restitution, and predatory-offender registration. He was separately charged in 2025 with violating a restraining order.
description: A woman sued former Chisago County Sheriff Richard Duncan and Chisago County in 2023 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, bringing civil rights claims under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983. Duncan, while sheriff, told the woman that a blackmailer was demanding she engage in sexual conduct with him; he later admitted he had fabricated the blackmail letters himself to coerce her into sex, and in November 2023 he pleaded guilty to one count of third-degree criminal sexual conduct. The suit alleged Duncan used his law enforcement authority, uniform, and vehicle in the scheme, and the court ruled the county could be held liable for his conduct. In February 2026, the county board approved a $7.5 million settlement, paid through the Minnesota Counties Intergovernmental Trust, in exchange for dismissal of the case.
notes: Seed data suggested a 2024 filing, but Minnesota Lawyer and Chisago County Press reporting states the federal suit was filed in 2023; the given slug is retained as assigned. The plaintiff has spoken publicly in named press interviews but is not named here per victim-naming rule.
